## Motivation

The Python HiCache storage pipeline runs one query, one transfer, one sync and one backup daemon thread per rank, and the query thread and the sync thread each rank-reduce their result with a gloo `all_reduce` on dedicated storage sync groups (`cache_controller.py` `_sync_prefetch_hit_query`, `_reduce_prefetch_ack`; `hybrid_cache_controller.py` overrides; since #43344 the PP ticket thread issues the same hit reduction). Those collectives are outside every `try/except`, and nothing on the scheduler thread checks whether the workers are alive. So when one rank's backend call hangs (slow `exists()`/`get()`, a stuck RPC) the peers block in the collective, and once the group timeout fires the collective raises and **kills the worker thread on every rank** (the healthy rank with `Timed out waiting ... for recv operation`, the hung rank with `Connection closed by peer` when it finally enters the collective). From then on no query or ack is ever published on any rank: under `wait_complete` every later L3-hit request waits forever, under `timeout` every one of them pays the full deadline and recomputes, and the only operator remedy (`/flush_cache`, detach) raises out of the scheduler. #43550 only guards the backend call, not the collective. The same strand happens when a worker thread dies for any other reason on one rank: its peers' collectives never complete.

Two-rank CPU reproduction (gloo, rank 1 hung in `batch_exists`, 3 s group timeout): rank 0's query thread dies at 3.0 s, rank 1's at 5.0 s the instant its call returns, nothing is published, every later query stays queued — on upstream main as well as with #43550.

This PR makes the worker collectives recoverable and gives the scheduler a rank-agreed liveness signal, so a collective failure or a dead worker degrades to "L3 unavailable" instead of silently stranding every rank.

## Modifications

**Worker threads (`cache_controller.py`, `hybrid_cache_controller.py`)**

- Every worker-thread collective goes through `HiCacheController._storage_sync_all_reduce`: on a `RuntimeError` (gloo timeout, connection closed) it logs one ERROR with the traceback, sets the controller-level `storage_sync_failed` flag and returns `False`; the caller publishes the operation as FAILED on this rank (hit query -> 0 hits with no pool verdict, transfer ack -> 0 completed tokens, sidecar ack -> all-zero pool hits) and **the thread stays alive**. Every later collective is still entered: gloo keeps a timed-out pair closed, so a broken group raises at once on every rank (measured 0.00-0.01 s), whereas skipping it would strand a peer on a group that did not fail (the hits and completion groups are distinct gloo groups even on TP2). The publication sequence stays exactly one per query and one ack per transfer batch, which is what the scheduler's MIN-of-queue-sizes drain relies on.
- The PP ticket thread (`pp_prefetch_command_thread_func`) runs the hit query and its MIN itself since #43344, so the guarded `_sync_prefetch_hit_query` covers the ticket path; an unexpected ticket failure records the same sync failure before the thread exits (the broadcast is the PP agreement itself). `is_pp_prefetch_ready` no longer raises for a dead ticket thread under the default policy (the health bit retires the ticket instead; `raise` keeps the old fail-loud behaviour), and `take_ready_pp_prefetch` waits in 1 s slices and raises when the local ticket thread is dead instead of blocking the scheduler forever on a ticket PP0 declared ready.
- `storage_workers_healthy()` / `storage_health_reason()`: rank-local liveness = no sync failure and every **started** storage worker thread (plus the PP ticket thread when present) alive. A controller whose storage I/O runs outside these Python workers has none to watch and reports healthy on their account.
- Two keys in `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config`, popped and validated at the top of `attach_storage_backend` before any side effect (that entry point also covers the decode offload manager, which bypasses `parse_storage_backend_extra_config`): `storage_failure_policy` (`"disable"` default, `"raise"`) and `storage_sync_timeout` (seconds, **default 300**; torch's gloo default is 30 minutes). The timeout is plumbed through a new optional `timeout` argument of `create_custom_parallel_group` into `torch.distributed.new_group` for the groups the controller builds in `_create_sync_groups` and for the PP ticket broadcast group, which is now created when the storage workers start — after attach has applied the timeout — instead of before the config is parsed (`reset()` restarts the threads and keeps the group). `mla_host_dedup._prebuild_prefetch_sync_groups` builds a second, currently unused set with torch's default.

**Scheduler thread (`unified_radix_cache.py`)**

- The health bit is folded into the collectives the drain already issues: `_sync_hicache_ready_counts` and `drain_storage_control_queues` append `int(cc.storage_workers_healthy())` to the MIN-reduced count tensor, read after the queue sizes (see below), on both the gloo reduce and the shared-memory count exchange (`_shm_count_exchange`; its `hicache` row grows from 8 to 9 words so the no-extra-pool layout keeps taking the shm path, `get_shm_exchange` gains a `width` argument for that). In buffer-only PP>1 *without* PP tickets every stage issues its own prefetch and `check_prefetch_progress` must cut on one value, so PP0's verdict is relayed with the existing `_pp_sync` (one recv per tick on PP>0, the coupling cache-mode PP already has); with PP tickets PP0 decides per request through the existing MAX, so stages keep their own bit and nothing new touches the PP group.
- `_apply_storage_health`: when the agreed bit drops (once): ERROR log with the reason (this rank's, or "reported by a peer rank"), `sglang:hicache_storage_healthy` gauge -> 0 (also set to 0 on detach, 1 on attach), then the policy. `disable` sets `storage_unavailable` and logs a WARNING once a minute while degraded; `raise` raises `RuntimeError` out of the scheduler.
- Under `storage_unavailable`: `prefetch_from_storage` and `query_storage_hit_length` return immediately, `write_backup_storage` / `enqueue_backup_intent` enqueue nothing new, `check_prefetch_progress` cuts every in-flight prefetch through the `deadline_expired` machinery of #44614 (no retry re-arm, no belief learning, no miss accounting) and reports it under a new `storage_unavailable` reason of `sglang:storage_prefetch_unfulfilled_tokens_total`, a PP ticket is retired on every rank through the PP0-decided MAX (verdict 0 pending / 1 ready / 2 retire), the drain reads every popped hit as a miss and applies no further transfer progress (completion still releases each operation's tail at the last agreed progress), and `_invalidate_absent_from_hit_query` learns nothing. Re-attaching the backend (fresh threads and groups) clears the flag; `/flush_cache` restarts the workers but keeps the groups, so it logs that L3 stays disabled.

**Why the degrade is rank-consistent.** After the first failure every collective on the broken group fails on every rank, but the failing collective itself can end differently per rank: a peer whose data arrived just before the timeout may complete while the other rank raised. The design therefore never trusts a value published around the failure: a worker sets `storage_sync_failed` *before* it publishes the failed item, and the scheduler reads the queue sizes *before* the health bit, so any round that counts (and thus pops) a possibly-asymmetric publication is a round in which the agreed bit is already 0 on every rank (MIN), and in such a round every rank discards the hit, freezes transfer progress and skips belief healing identically. Items drained in earlier rounds were reduced successfully on all ranks. The frozen progress is conservative (a batch that every rank did complete may be dropped) but identical everywhere; the prefix that was already agreed is still used.

**Why `disable` is the default.** The OSS default stack has no supervisor that restarts a crashed server, and a degraded L3 (one ERROR, a gauge at 0, a WARNING per minute, cold TTFT) is strictly better than today's strand or a crash of the whole engine; fleets that alert on crashes rather than logs can opt into `raise`. Happy to flip the default if maintainers prefer fail-loud.

**Why 300 s.** The group timeout only bounds how long a healthy rank waits for a peer that is stuck in its backend; tripping it degrades L3 until re-attach, so it must stay far above any healthy batch call (128 pages per call) and above the 60 s idle ticket broadcast, while noticing a hung peer in minutes rather than after 30. A per-call bound that turns a hung call into a single miss without touching the group is a separate PR (#44343).

**Known limits** (pre-existing behaviour, called out for reviewers): the health bit is agreed over the ranks that share a scheduler drain, so in every PP>1 shape a PP>0 stage's own worker failure reaches PP0 only once a cross-stage sync collective fails or times out (folding PP>0 bits needs a reverse message per tick; follow-up). A worker stuck inside a backend call (not a collective) is still only released by that call returning or by a per-call bound (#44343); the health bit covers thread death and collective failure. `/flush_cache`/detach while a worker is still inside a hung backend call still fail their 10 s join (flush raises out of the scheduler, pre-existing; #44348); once the call returns both succeed. A worker that dies loses the acks it had not published, so its in-flight operation's host tail stays allocated until re-attach; under a dead backup thread, cache-mode `ongoing_backup` host locks and already-queued buffer-mode write staging stay pinned until re-attach (only new work is gated).

The GPU runs below were done on the first revision of this PR; the rebased code was validated on CPU (below).

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward changes. On the GPU runs below (first revision), L3-hit outputs match the cold greedy outputs (3/3 verify prompts, 0 mismatches).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout` | 16/16 (99.0 % cached) | 0.128 / 0.191 / 0.244 s | 1 on both ranks |
| `wait_complete` | 16/16 (99.0 % cached) | 0.129 / 0.203 / 0.245 s | 1 on both ranks |

 - **`--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config HICACHE_STORAGE_BACKEND_EXTRA_CONFIG`**: the extra config can be either
   - a JSON string containing extra configuration for the storage backend, e.g., `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"prefetch_threshold":512, "prefetch_timeout_base": 0.5, "prefetch_timeout_per_ki_token": 0.25}' `, or

+  - Two keys configure the storage worker liveness handling and are consumed before the backend sees the config. `storage_failure_policy` (`"disable"`, the default, or `"raise"`) selects what the scheduler does once the rank-agreed storage health bit drops because a storage worker thread exited or a cross-rank sync collective failed (e.g. a gloo timeout while a peer rank is stuck in its backend): `disable` degrades to no-L3 (new prefetches and backups are skipped, in-flight prefetches resolve as misses, the `sglang:hicache_storage_healthy` gauge drops to 0) until the storage backend is detached and re-attached; `raise` fails the scheduler. `storage_sync_timeout` (seconds, default 300) bounds those sync collectives (the worker threads' hit/ack reductions and, with PP prefetch tickets, the ticket broadcast and the ticket thread's hit reduction), so a hung peer is detected after that long instead of after torch's 30-minute gloo default. Keep it well above the slowest single backend call any rank can see: a slow but healthy `exists()`/`get()` on one rank that exceeds it trips its peers' collectives and degrades L3 until the backend is re-attached. The health bit is agreed over the ranks that share a scheduler drain: in PP>1 deployments a PP>0 stage's own worker failure reaches PP0 only once a cross-stage sync collective fails or times out.

+class _HoldingBackend:
+    """batch_exists blocks on `hold` for the first call when hold_first; every
+    call reports all pages present."""

+    def __init__(self, hold_first: bool):

+        self.hold = threading.Event()
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def batch_exists(self, hashes, extra_info=None):
+        self.calls += 1
+        if self.hold_first and self.calls == 1:
+            self.hold.wait()

+def _idle_thread(stop_event: threading.Event) -> threading.Thread:

+def _operation(rid: str, host_indices=None) -> PrefetchOperation:
+    operation = PrefetchOperation(CacheRequestHandle(rid, 0), TOKENS)
+    operation.stats_requested_tokens = len(TOKENS)
+    operation.host_indices = host_indices
+    return operation

+def _track(cache, operation) -> None:
+    cache.ongoing_prefetch[operation.handle] = _OngoingPrefetch(
+        0, RadixKey(array("q", TOKENS)), operation.host_indices, operation, None, {}
+    )
+
+
+def _ack(operation, completed=None, done=False) -> PrefetchAck:
+    return PrefetchAck(
+        rid=operation.request_id,
+        operation=operation,
+        completed_tokens=completed,
+        completed_req=True if done else None,
+    )

+
+def _drain(queue: Queue, want: int, budget_s: float) -> list:
+    items = []
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + budget_s
+    while len(items) < want and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            items.append(queue.get(timeout=0.05))
+        except Empty:
+            continue
+    return items
+
+
+def _same_on_every_rank(snapshot):
+    snapshots = [None] * dist.get_world_size()
+    dist.all_gather_object(snapshots, snapshot)
+    assert all(other == snapshots[0] for other in snapshots), snapshots
+    return snapshots[0]
+
+
+def _wait_for(predicate, budget_s: float) -> None:
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    while not predicate():
+        assert time.monotonic() - t0 < budget_s, "condition not met in time"
+        time.sleep(0.02)
+
+
+def _sync_groups():
+    """Fresh (failing, healthy) gloo groups, created collectively."""
+    failing = dist.new_group(backend="gloo", timeout=timedelta(seconds=SYNC_TIMEOUT_S))
+    healthy = dist.new_group(
+        backend="gloo", timeout=timedelta(seconds=HEALTHY_TIMEOUT_S)
+    )
+    return failing, healthy
+
+
+def _start_workers(cc) -> tuple[threading.Thread, threading.Thread]:
+    query_thread = threading.Thread(target=cc.prefetch_thread_func, daemon=True)
+    sync_thread = threading.Thread(target=cc.prefetch_sync_thread_func, daemon=True)
+    query_thread.start()
+    sync_thread.start()
+    cc.prefetch_thread, cc.prefetch_sync_thread = query_thread, sync_thread
+    return query_thread, sync_thread
+
+
+def _stop(cc, *workers) -> None:
+    cc.storage_stop_event.set()
+    cc.prefetch_queue.put(None)
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(None)
+    for worker in workers:
+        worker.join(5)

+def _hit_query_timeout_body(rank: int) -> None:
+    """Rank 1 hangs in its backend; rank 0's hit MIN times out. Both query
+    threads must survive, the untouched completion group must stay usable on
+    both ranks, and check_hicache_events must degrade every rank at once."""
+    hits_group, completion_group = _sync_groups()
+    backend = _HoldingBackend(hold_first=(rank == 1))
+    cc = _controller(hits_group, completion_group, backend)
+    get_storage_hash_str(TOKENS, None, page_size=PAGE)  # JIT warm-up off the clock
+    query_thread, sync_thread = _start_workers(cc)
+    cache = _scheduler_cache(cc)
+    dist.barrier()
+
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    ops = [_operation("op1"), _operation("op2")]
+    for operation in ops:
+        _track(cache, operation)
+        cc.prefetch_queue.put(operation)
+    if rank == 0:
+        _wait_for(lambda: cc.storage_sync_failed, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    # Cross-group: rank 1's query thread is still hung and rank 0 has already
+    # failed on the hits group, yet an ack on the completion group must still
+    # reduce promptly on both ranks (a peer that skipped it would strand this
+    # rank for that group's whole timeout).
+    dist.barrier()
+    transfer = _operation("xfer", host_indices=torch.arange(BATCH_TOKENS))
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(transfer, BATCH_TOKENS - rank * 10))
+    acks = _drain(cc.ack_prefetch_queue, want=1, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    assert [(a.rid, a.completed_tokens) for a in acks] == [
+        ("xfer", BATCH_TOKENS - 10)
+    ], acks
+    if rank == 1:
+        time.sleep(max(0.0, HOLD_S - (time.monotonic() - t0)))
+        backend.hold.set()
+    published = _drain(cc.prefetch_hit_queue, want=2, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    published_at = time.monotonic() - t0
+    # The hung rank's own collective fails as soon as it enters (the peer's
+    # timeout closed the pair), so op 1 is a published miss on both ranks and
+    # the query thread is alive to serve op 2: a retry on the broken group
+    # fails at once instead of waiting out another timeout.
+    assert [(op.request_id, op.storage_hit_count) for op in published] == [
+        ("op1", 0),
+        ("op2", 0),
+    ], published
+    assert published_at < (SYNC_TIMEOUT_S if rank == 0 else HOLD_S) + FAST_S / 2
+    assert query_thread.is_alive() and sync_thread.is_alive()
+    assert cc.storage_sync_failed and not cc.storage_workers_healthy()
+    op3 = _operation("op3")
+    _track(cache, op3)
+    cc.prefetch_queue.put(op3)
+    assert [op.request_id for op in _drain(cc.prefetch_hit_queue, 1, FAST_S)] == ["op3"]
+    for operation in published + [op3]:
+        cc.prefetch_hit_queue.put(operation)
+
+    # Scheduler side, the production round: the MIN-reduced health bit
+    # degrades every rank in the same tick; the drained queries resolve as
+    # misses, an unpublished prefetch is cut, and no new prefetch is issued.
+    op4 = _operation("op4")
+    _track(cache, op4)
+    cache.check_hicache_events()
+    assert cache.storage_unavailable
+    revoked = [
+        call.args[0].rid for call in cache.revoke_pending_prefetch.call_args_list
+    ]
+    assert revoked == ["op1", "op2", "op3"], revoked
+    assert cache.check_prefetch_progress(op4.handle)
+    assert op4.is_terminated()
+    assert cache.revoke_pending_prefetch.call_args.args[0] == op4.handle
+    assert cache.prefetch_from_storage(CacheRequestHandle("op5", 0), 0, TOKENS) is None
+    assert cc.prefetch_queue.empty()
+    _same_on_every_rank(
+        (
+            revoked,
+            cache._prefetch_outcome_stats["revoked_full_miss"],
+            cache._prefetch_outcome_stats["l3_miss_tokens"],
+        )
+    )
+
+    # The raise policy fails the scheduler loudly on the same evidence.
+    cc.storage_failure_policy = "raise"
+    loud = _scheduler_cache(cc)
+    try:
+        loud.check_hicache_events()
+    except RuntimeError as e:
+        assert "unhealthy" in str(e), e
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError("raise policy did not fail the drain")
+    _stop(cc, query_thread, sync_thread)
+

+def _ack_alignment_body(rank: int) -> None:
+    """A completion-group timeout mid-transfer: one ack per batch still
+    reaches the scheduler on every rank, in order; progress freezes at the
+    last agreed value and each completion finishes its own operation."""
+    completion_group, hits_group = _sync_groups()
+    cc = _controller(hits_group, completion_group, _HoldingBackend(hold_first=False))
+    query_thread, sync_thread = _start_workers(cc)
+    cache = _scheduler_cache(cc)
+    op_a = _operation("A", host_indices=torch.arange(3 * BATCH_TOKENS))
+    op_b = _operation("B", host_indices=torch.arange(BATCH_TOKENS))
+    for operation in (op_a, op_b):
+        _track(cache, operation)
+
+    dist.barrier()
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_a, BATCH_TOKENS))
+    _wait_for(lambda: cc.ack_prefetch_queue.qsize() == 1, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    cache.check_hicache_events()  # healthy round: the agreed progress lands
+    assert (op_a.completed_tokens, cache.storage_unavailable) == (BATCH_TOKENS, False)
+    if rank == 1:
+        time.sleep(HOLD_S)  # this rank's IO thread is stuck for batch 2
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_a, 2 * BATCH_TOKENS - rank * 10))
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_a, 3 * BATCH_TOKENS))
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_a, done=True))
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_b, BATCH_TOKENS))
+    cc.prefetch_sync_queue.put(_ack(op_b, done=True))
+    acks = _drain(cc.ack_prefetch_queue, want=5, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    sequence = [(a.rid, a.completed_tokens, bool(a.completed_req)) for a in acks]
+    assert sequence == [
+        ("A", 0, False),
+        ("A", 0, False),
+        ("A", None, True),
+        ("B", 0, False),
+        ("B", None, True),
+    ], sequence
+    assert sync_thread.is_alive() and cc.storage_sync_failed
+    _same_on_every_rank(sequence)
+    # Cross-group: the hits group did not fail, so a query still reduces
+    # promptly on both ranks and keeps its agreed value.
+    dist.barrier()
+    query = _operation("after")
+    _track(cache, query)
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    cc.prefetch_queue.put(query)
+    hits = _drain(cc.prefetch_hit_queue, want=1, budget_s=FAST_S)
+    assert time.monotonic() - t0 < FAST_S / 2
+    assert [(op.request_id, op.storage_hit_count) for op in hits] == [
+        ("after", len(TOKENS))
+    ], hits
+
+    # Degraded round: no progress is applied from the failed acks, each
+    # completion finishes its own operation and releases the right tail, and
+    # the agreed hit reads as a miss.
+    for ack in acks:
+        cc.ack_prefetch_queue.put(ack)
+    cc.prefetch_hit_queue.put(hits[0])
+    cache.check_hicache_events()
+    assert cache.storage_unavailable
+    assert (op_a.completed_tokens, op_b.completed_tokens) == (BATCH_TOKENS, 0)
+    finished = [
+        call.args[0].request_id for call in cache._handle_prefetch_result.call_args_list
+    ]
+    assert finished == ["A", "B"], finished
+    released = [len(call.args[0]) for call in cc.append_host_mem_release.call_args_list]
+    assert released == [2 * BATCH_TOKENS, BATCH_TOKENS], released
+    assert cache.revoke_pending_prefetch.call_args.args[0] == query.handle
+    _stop(cc, query_thread, sync_thread)
+

+def _rank_main(rank: int, rendezvous: str) -> None:
+    # A regression that turns a recovery into a hang must fail, not block CI.
+    watchdog = threading.Timer(120, lambda: os._exit(86))
+    watchdog.daemon = True
